1.title: The Value of Data
1.text: Welcome to Module three: The Value of Data. It covers the exam area two. Exploring data transformation with Google Cloud. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do seven things. two point one Describe the intrinsic role that data plays in an organization's digital transformation: why data is valuable. Databases, data warehouses and data lakes. Types of data. The data supply chain. Data governance. Openness and interoperability. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: two. Exploring data transformation with Google Cloud (about eighteen percent). Exam format: ninety minutes and fifty to sixty multiple-choice questions. Validated against: the official Google Cloud Digital Leader exam guide.

1.title: Why data is valuable
1.text: Why data is valuable. Data becomes valuable when it is turned into action. Real-time business insights. See sales by store as it happens. Identifying trends. Spot seasonal demand before it peaks. Informing strategic decisions. Choose where to open the next shop. Fueling A I. Train models and ground agents in company data. Organizations can use data they already have, collect new data (sensors, apps, customer interactions) or source data from outside (partners, public data). Exam tip: Data is the fuel for analytics and A I. Better data means better decisions and better models.

1.title: Databases, data warehouses and data lakes
1.text: Databases, data warehouses and data lakes. The figure shows this: Database, data warehouse and data lake compared.

1.title: Databases, data warehouses and data lakes, continued
1.text: Databases, data warehouses and data lakes. Database. Holds: Current, structured records for applications. Best for: Transactions: orders, accounts, inventory. Data warehouse. Holds: Cleaned, structured data from many sources, organized for analysis. Best for: Reports, dashboards and business intelligence. Data lake. Holds: Raw data of any type (structured, semi-structured, unstructured) at low cost. Best for: Data science, machine learning and future uses.

1.title: Types of data
1.text: Types of data. First-party data. Your own data about your customers and operations. Second-party data. A partner's first-party data that you receive by agreement. Third-party data. Data bought or collected by an outside provider. Structured. Rows and columns with a fixed schema (tables). Semi-structured. Tags or keys but flexible shape (Jason, X M L, logs). Unstructured. No fixed format: images, video, audio, free text, documents. The cloud unlocks unstructured data, which is most of the world's data and was hard to use before.

1.title: The data supply chain
1.text: The data supply chain. Data genesis. Data is created (a purchase, a sensor reading). Data collection. Data is captured into systems. Data processing. Data is cleaned and transformed. Data storage. Data is kept in the right store. Data analysis. Data is analyzed for insight. Data activation. Insight is put to work: a decision, an alert, an A I action. Exam tip: Genesis, collection, processing, storage, analysis, activation. Activation is where value appears.

1.title: Data governance and openness
1.text: Data governance and openness. Data governance. The policies, roles and processes for data quality, access, security, privacy and compliance across its life. Why it matters. Trusted, secure, compliant data is needed for analytics and A I. Data silos. Data locked in separate systems that cannot be combined. Openness and interoperability. Open formats and standards let data move between platforms, remove silos and avoid vendor lock-in. Exam tip: Database for transactions, warehouse for analysis, lake for raw data. If a scenario says raw, any type, low cost, future use, the answer is the data lake.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. A bank processes customer account transactions all day and needs current, structured records for its apps. Which store fits best? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: A database for transactional records. Databases hold current structured records for transactional applications.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. An analyst needs one place with cleaned data from many systems for dashboards and reports. Which store fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: A data warehouse organized for analysis. A data warehouse holds cleaned, structured data from many sources for analysis.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. A company wants to keep raw video, text and sensor data cheaply for future machine learning. Which store fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: A data lake that holds raw data of any type. A data lake stores raw data of any type at low cost for future use.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. Customer purchase history that a retailer collected itself is called what? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: First-party data owned by the retailer. Data you collect about your own customers and operations is first-party data.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. In the data supply chain, which stage puts an insight to work, for example by triggering an alert? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Data activation, which uses the insight. Data activation is the final stage, where insight drives action.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. Why do open standards and interoperability matter for data platforms? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: They remove silos and help avoid vendor lock-in. Open formats let data move between platforms, which removes silos and avoids lock-in.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What is a data warehouse for? Answer: Analysis, reports and business intelligence on cleaned data. Question two. What does a data lake hold? Answer: Raw data of any type. Question three. What is first-party data? Answer: Your own data about your customers and operations.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. Name the six supply chain stages. Answer: Genesis, collection, processing, storage, analysis, activation. Question five. What is data governance? Answer: Policies and roles for data quality, access, security and compliance. Question six. What is a data silo? Answer: Data locked in a separate system that cannot be combined.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Value: insights, trends, decisions, fuel for A I. Stores: database (transactions), warehouse (analysis), lake (raw, any type). Types: first, second, third party; structured, semi-structured, unstructured. Supply chain: genesis, collection, processing, storage, analysis, activation. Governance: quality, access, security, compliance; openness removes silos and lock-in.
